originalTitle: Prick’s theatrical industrial punk is perfect for spooky season

content: While deep in the recording process for The Downward Spiral, Trent Reznor lent some of his production talents to old friend Kevin McMahon, from the new wave band Lucky Pierre (which Reznor was briefly a member of). While Reznor is only credited as the producer on four tracks off Prick’s self-titled debut record, his fingerprints are all over it. But McMahon also can’t suppress his inner theater kid, which also gives the songs the sort of glammy flamboyance found on T. Rex records. Prick embraces the inherent theatricality of goth in a way that Nine Inch Nails never did. Opener “Communiqué” is a fuzzy blast of simple punk riffs with electronic sprinklings on top. McMahon’s vocals occasionally detour from the half-spoken verses that sound borrowed from a musical to full-throated Al Jourgensen-esque screams. The rough-around-the-edges production and focus on live instrumentation feel like a prototype for what Reznor would eventually revisit on With Teeth. But it’s the second track, “Riverhead” where Reznor’s influences fully rear their head (even though he is not actually credited as the producer). The vocal melodies swerve like Outside- and Earthling-era Bowie around guitars that buzz with all the digital charr of the Broken EP. Then, around the three-minute mark, comes the breakdown. It slowly builds with layers of electronic drums, mechanical chords, and loping synthetic-sounding guitar melodies. The entire back chunk could easily have been a Downward Spiral or even The Fragile B-side. These moments of richly layered production, though, are almost always immediately undermined, as with the sloppy garage-punk intro of “Tough”. It’s these moments that make Prick so charming. It’s a serious record, but it never takes itself too seriously. McMahon isn’t afraid to get goofy (“Pink panties, blue panties, yellow panties. I’m gonna wrap around your nose, oh panty-ho-hose” he sings on “Other People”) and over-the-top with his vocal performances. He’s willing to let the guitar drift out of time, the bass strings rattle, and revels in industrial lo-fi. [Media: https://youtu.be/ppCyIdkoXGk] “Animal” is perhaps the best-known track from the album, its video having received at least some MTV airplay. It combines backward melodic samples reminiscent of “Closer” and follows a similar lyrical theme: > Consent is all I need To bring out the savage in me Your scent is all I need To bring out the animal in me But where “Closer” opts for slinky disco sleaze, “Animal” is all raw shouted desire. “I Apologize” is the most scatter-brained track on the album, and for that reason, one of my favorites. It opens with awkward whip-crack-like percussion and McMahon singing slightly flat and unaffected, before briefly taking off into a jangly new wave verse that quickly morphs into a hard-rock stop in the chorus. But that’s short-lived as well. The second verse is all “Space Oddity”-era Bowie acoustic strums, then there’s a solo that sounds like an arcade machine on the verge of meltdown. That then drops into a Ministry-esque dirge of layered guitars and screams. The song then returns to the chorus, but keeps adding elements until it’s stuffed to capacity and collapses on itself. Prick’s self-titled record has plenty in common with other ‘90s industrial acts. But McMahon is clearly having a lot more fun than many of his contemporaries, and that helps elevate it above the myriad Nine Inch Nails wannabes out there. Prick is available on most major streaming services, including Apple Music, Spotify, Qobuz, Deezer, and YouTube Music.
chineseTitle: Prick 的戏剧工业朋克风格非常适合恐怖季节
chineseSummary: 在深入《The Downward Spiral》的录音过程中，特伦特·雷兹诺 (Trent Reznor) 将自己的一些制作才能借给了来自新浪潮乐队 Lucky Pierre（雷兹诺曾短暂加入）的老朋友凯文·麦克马洪 (Kevin McMahon)。虽然 Reznor 只被认为是 Prick 同名首张唱片中四首曲目的制作人，但他的指纹 [...]
chineseContent: 在深入《The Downward Spiral》的录音过程中，特伦特·雷兹诺 (Trent Reznor) 将自己的一些制作才能借给了来自新浪潮乐队 Lucky Pierre（雷兹诺曾短暂加入）的老朋友凯文·麦克马洪 (Kevin McMahon)。虽然雷兹诺只被认为是普里克首张同名唱片中四首歌曲的制作人，但他的指纹无处不在。但麦克马洪也无法抑制他内心的戏剧孩子，这也给这些歌曲带来了霸王龙唱片上那种华丽的华丽感。普里克以九寸钉从未做过的方式拥抱哥特固有的戏剧性。开场曲“Communiqué”是简单朋克连复段的模糊爆炸，顶部有电子音乐。麦克马洪的歌声偶尔会从音乐剧中借用的半言半语的诗句转向阿尔·约根森式的大声尖叫。粗糙的制作和对现场乐器的关注感觉就像 Reznor 最终在《With Teeth》中重新审视的原型。但在第二首歌曲《Riverhead》中，雷兹诺的影响力得到了充分体现（尽管他实际上并未被认为是制作人）。人声旋律像地球时代和地球时代的鲍伊一样，围绕着吉他旋转，伴随着《Broken EP》的所有数字魅力。然后，大约三分钟左右，崩溃出现了。它慢慢地由电子鼓、机械和弦和跳跃的合成吉他旋律层层构建。整个后部块很可能是一个向下螺旋，甚至是脆弱的 B 面。然而，这些层次丰富的制作时刻几乎总是立即被破坏，就像“Tough”中草率的车库朋克介绍一样。正是这些时刻让普里克如此迷人。这是一张严肃的唱片，但它从不把自己看得太严肃。麦克马洪并不害怕变得愚蠢
